catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue motion class carries the coupled six-component SmarPod pose in its native unit: cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 fixes position in mm and orientation in rad, and cap.motion.joint_position.v1 fixes rad, while the clone states no engineering unit for any pose component (README.md:1-13, src/SmarPodMain.py:45-53) and converting without one would invent a unit. The vendor pose is the platform pose read by smarpod.GetPose, not a tool-centre-point Cartesian command or a joint vector.

notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names the OphydDriver helper, but the upstream entry is a custom ophyd Signal subclass (src/OphydSmarPod.py:65) that reads and writes the vendor smaract.smarpod API (GetPose, Move, IsPoseReachable, Stop); the OphydDriver profile accepts only direct classic Component(EpicsSignal|EpicsSignalRO|Signal, literal) declarations and cannot express custom Signal classes. This package is therefore a direct Driver over the same entry symbol, with the production adapter in native.py and the fake in fake.py. Gate G7 reports one expected warning, G7.MAYBE_ABSENT for the extra public name stop: SmarSignal itself has no stop method; the vendor stop is the module call smarpod.Stop(handle) used at src/SmarPodMain.py:109, and both the real adapter and the fake expose it as stop so the driver has exactly one native stop path. The clone's stop route is a software stop of commanded motion followed by a fresh GetMoveStatus check for MoveStatus.STOPPED (src/SmarPodMain.py:109-121); it is exposed as the safe-state action cap.motion.stop.v1 and reached by @estop. The clone contains no text about a physical emergency stop, so estop_physical_ref is absent and no physical e-stop is claimed.

The pose unit is not stated anywhere in the clone; the fields use the dimensionless UCUM code 1 and say that the value is in the controller's native unit, and no conversion is performed. The clone also states no travel range or workspace bound; reachability is only the run-time IsPoseReachable check (src/OphydSmarPod.py:96-104), so both pose inputs are Limit.operator_required and refuse with MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the site supplies an envelope. site-limits.example.json is an example only: it uses the range [-1, 1] so the fake conformance suite's synthesized pose completes; it is not a device fact or a recommended workspace and a site must replace it with its measured envelope.

Calibration and reference-mark search are deliberately not performed by native.py: the upstream set_up runs Calibrate and FindReferenceMarks (src/SmarPodMain.py:87-95), which move the platform without an MHS command and outside the operator envelope. The hardware adapter opens the controller, refuses an unreferenced one, and applies the upstream motion configuration (speed, frequency, relative pivot, coordinate system); the primary pose read/write interface is preserved. The concurrent Stop call from the e-stop thread while Move is in progress has not been verified against vendor documentation, so this backend remains unreviewed.

The fake is an analytic stand-in, not a recording: it keeps the SmarSignal surface (get, set, get_status, trigger, check_pose, verify_stopped_status, verify_reachable_position, tear_down) plus stop, simulates a 50 ms travel in 5 ms steps, and every starting value, duration and poll interval is marked placeholder test data. The fake backend is served as F0 contract_checked evidence; the hardware backend was never run and this package is model-authored and unreviewed (reviewed_by is null), so the loader refuses the hardware backend at R2 until a human signs it. The stop_motion deceleration field is accepted for class schema compatibility only; the vendor Stop(handle) call has no deceleration argument, so the value is not passed through and the controller's own stop profile is used.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct-Driver deviation against the readiness evidence (blocked for OphydDriver: the entries are custom Signal subclasses, src/OphydSmarPod.py:65-132): a direct Driver with a native.py adapter over the binary vendor module smaract.smarpod is a sound route to the repository's primary device, R2 fits a hexapod, and the stop holds in kind: the upstream's own smarpod.Stop(handle) followed by a fresh GetMoveStatus check for STOPPED (src/SmarPodMain.py:109-121), which the safe-state action cap.motion.stop.v1 repeats with a fresh-status poll of up to 5 s, so an e-stop completes only when the controller reports STOPPED within the 1 s e-stop budget. A probe with a controller that keeps moving after Stop (review/lists/r24-probe_smarpod_running_move.py) ends the e-stop MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED after 1.01 s with the latch held, so the outcome stays honest; the author's fake stop() marks the platform stopped at once and ends its own move, which the clone does not show the vendor Move(handle, pose, 0, True) doing. The G7.MAYBE_ABSENT warning for stop is true (ophyd's Signal defines no stop, labs/bluesky/ophyd/ophyd/signal.py:79): stop is the adapter's vendor module call, not a SmarSignal member. Defects fixed: the pose_to_double_list fact cited src/OphydSmarPod.py:45-53 (a describe() body) instead of src/SmarPodMain.py:45-53; the set_up fact took model 10052 and the locator from 70-124 (they are on 8-9); the trigger fact said trigger waits for STOPPED although its loop never re-reads the status (55-62); the pose descriptions now say that the unit '1', which G8 requires on a hardware numeric input (removing it fails G8.NO_UNIT), is a placeholder and not a dimensionless claim, which supersedes the author's note on the dimensionless code. The reviewer changed driver.py (docstring, the POSE_UNIT comment and description, three facts corrected and three added: the class attributes at src/SmarPodMain.py:8-9, set_up's except clause that does not re-raise at 126-133, SmarSignalDifferentAxis.set at src/OphydSmarPod.py:107-114), facts.md and site-limits.example.json (unit dropped, a note that one envelope bounds all six components), and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the gate and collect.py --strict pass with the digest unchanged (sha256:6c231c210cd2954a18cbad1050862ca892a44293e019eac934e0a02e5d9c4951). The card's ophyd family does not fit this repository: override proposal direct-driver python-object. For the human reviewer: R2 hexapod; the loader refuses the hardware backend until a human signs. native.py is the author's own adapter over smaract.smarpod (not in the clone), not the upstream SmarSignal: check in SmarAct's SmarPod documentation that Stop(handle) from the e-stop thread ends a Move(handle, pose, 0, True) blocking in another thread, that concurrent calls on one handle are safe, and the pose units (positions and rotations share one operator envelope). On every connect the adapter applies the upstream author's site settings (SetSpeed 1, 3e-3; SetMaxFrequency 18500; relative pivot [10e-3, 0, 0]; coordinate system Pose(0, 0, 0, 1.5, 0, 0), src/SmarPodMain.py:55-68), which define the frame of every pose and envelope, and it refuses an unreferenced controller instead of running the upstream's automatic Calibrate and FindReferenceMarks motion. Never use the upstream single-axis classes: each set builds a new SmarSignalRO whose constructor runs set_up, i.e. calibration and referencing (src/OphydSmarPod.py:14-20, 107-114). A cancelled move receipt does not mean the platform did not move, and teardown closes the controller without a stop.
